title: Finance Assistant
description:
Main purpose of job Finance Assistant

To be responsible to the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) for the delivery of a quality cashier service.

To assist with managing the councils cash resources and bank accounts in line with the needs of user departments.

Summary of responsibilities and personal duties Finance Assistant
- To assist the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with tasks relating to the management of the cashier service including its bank accounts.
- To assist the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with the updating of appropriate policies, regulations and legislation.
- To provide advice and guidance to user departments and suppliers with regard to the cashier service.
- To liaise with the appropriate bank(s) under the direction of the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with regard to banking facilities and queries.
- To administer payroll deductions and ensure timely payment to recipients, for example, Inland Revenue, NILGOSC, Trade Unions and other relevant bodies.
- To process payments in relation to Accounts Payable and Payroll transactions.
- To assist with the administration and preparation of statistical reports relating to the Cashiers Imprest Bank Account, Euro Bank Account and other bank accounts relevant to the cashier service.
- To assist the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with maintaining, updating and monitoring a list of the councils bank accounts.
- To assist with the Bankers Automatic Clearing Systems (BACS) on behalf of the council by liaising with the sponsor, BACS and Digital Services in respect of new developments.
- To assist with the implementation of best value and quality improvements.
- To make recommendations to the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with regard to developing and improving the service.
- To participate in all induction and in-service training provided by Belfast City Council and in the induction and support of all newly appointed staff and other human resource management policies and procedures, as appropriate, including, absence management, disciplinary and grievance procedure.
- To act in accordance with the council and departmental policies and procedures including customer care, equal opportunities, health and safety, safeguarding and any pertinent legislation.
- To undertake the duties in such a way as to enhance and protect the reputation and public profile of the council.
- To undertake such other relevant duties as may from time to time be required.

Experience Finance Assistant

Applicants must, as at the closing date for receipt of application forms, be able to demonstrate, by providing personal and specific examples on the application form, at least one years relevant experience in each of the following areas:
- working in a financial environment and dealing with reconciliation of payments in 1 a large public or private sector organisation;
- using Microsoft Office IT applications and financial packages used for the processing of BACS payments; and
- working in a busy office environment as part of a team, using prioritisation skills to adhere to strict deadlines.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Join Fieldfisher as a Credit Controller!

What can you expect?

Join Fieldfisher's innovative Belfast office, located in our new premises in the Adelaide Exchange Building, Adelaide Street Belfast. As a Credit Controller, you will support the Credit Control Supervisor and collaborate with the revenue control, billing, and cashiers teams. Fieldfisher is known for delivering first-class, commercially focused results through a balanced mix of legal technology solutions and highly skilled resources. If you are professional, driven, and able to meet deadlines under pressure, we would love to hear from you.

Responsibilities
- Have Daily involvement and provide support to the Credit Control Supervisor whilst having some cross over with the revenue control, billing and cashiers teams
- Provide support to our Partners and Lawyers
- Manage the distribution of partners reports
- Telephone clients on a daily basis
- Maintain adequate records of conversations with partners/clients on credit control and actions arising from meetings and conversations
- Being proactive, setting diary notes to follow up with partners fee earners
- Have a good understanding of double entry book keeping and understanding client files
- Have responsibility of reconciliations of ledgers and preparing statements/cash reconciliations for both internal and external use
- Responsibility of ensuring that all requests from clients are actioned and follow up
- Advise on whether balances in client account can be used to settle bills raised
- Develop strong working relationships with Partners and working capital team members
- Buddy up with another CC to offer cover / resourcing as and when needed

Who are we looking for?
- We don't have a type. We believe our differences are our strength; varied cultures, approaches and experience can only benefit us.

What do we offer?
- You can be yourself: It takes everyone to make us who we are. We're a culture of diverse perspectives, with each of us making unique contributions that make us better together.
- In the office or WFH?: We think the best balance is more time in the office than at home, so we operate a 60:40 rule.
- Beyond salary: We offer plenty of benefits; private medical insurance, health cash plan, dental insurance, life assurance, critical illness insurance, matched pension contributions up to 7%, holiday trading, plus many more.
- Modern Office Space: Located at Adelaide Exchange, Belfast City Centre, with excellent commuter links and parking nearby.
- Nurturing your talent: Take a 'build a career' approach to your training. You'll be on a pathway but free to wander if you see something you'd like to study more closely.
- Funnel your interests: You have a life outside work, and we can help it to flourish. Join clubs, affinity networks, inclusive events, and pro bono/charity initiatives.

Why join Fieldfisher?

At Fieldfisher, we know people do their best work when they feel supported, valued and able to be themselves.

We invest in helping our people build fulfilling careers while maintaining a healthy balance with life outside work. From professional development opportunities and wellbeing initiatives to flexible ways of working, we're committed to creating an environment where people can thrive.

As part of our People First approach, we offer a range of support for colleagues and their families. Find out more about our family-friendly approach.

Inclusion at Fieldfisher

We want everyone at Fieldfisher to feel respected, valued and able to succeed.

We're committed to attracting, developing and retaining talented people from all backgrounds and creating opportunities for colleagues to grow and thrive. We believe that different experiences and perspectives strengthen our firm, our teams and the service we provide to clients.

Our Inclusion Networks, colleague-led initiatives, awareness campaigns and learning programmes help build community, encourage understanding and support an environment where everyone feels they belong.

Fieldfisher is proud to be an Opening Doors Employer with Business in the Community Northern Ireland. Through our inclusion and recruitment strategies, we are committed to broadening access to careers, attracting talent from diverse backgrounds, and creating a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

Accessibility and adjustments

We're committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require any adjustments during your application or interview we'll work with you to understand what support you need and ensure you can participate fully in the process.

What to do next:
- Click 'Apply Now', complete an online application and upload a CV. Please note that CVs will not be accepted via email in line with our data privacy policy.
- Successful applications will be invited to a 20-30-minute introductory call with a recruiter.
- Every role recruits differently. But we'll always let you know what to expect from the process, so you get no surprises.
- For hybrid opportunities, you'll be invited to visit our offices for a face-to-face meeting.
- We try to make sure the process takes around 2-3 weeks only, but we can't always promise that. We will work around everyone's availability.

We recruit on a rolling basis. Your application may be reviewed before the application deadline. We accept applications until we have filled the role.

title: Supply Chain Coordinator
company: CBSbutler Holdings Limited trading as CBSbutler - Agency - Contract
description:
Supply Chain Coordinator

Location: Belfast

Working Arrangement: Fully on-site

The Opportunity

An exciting opportunity has arisen to join a leading global organisation within its Supply Chain Operations team as a Supply Chain Coordinator, based in Belfast.

Operating within a complex, international supply chain supporting multiple manufacturing programmes, you will manage a portfolio of suppliers, taking responsibility for supplier performance, material availability and the smooth flow of goods throughout the end-to-end supply chain.

Working in a fast-paced, digitally enabled manufacturing environment, you will play a key role in identifying and mitigating supply risks, managing demand and forecasts, resolving supplier issues and ensuring operational requirements are met.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience in supply chain, procurement or manufacturing who enjoys problem-solving, working with suppliers and driving continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage a portfolio of suppliers on a day-to-day basis, monitoring performance and ensuring supply chain requirements are met.
- Proactively identify supply risks, anticipate potential disruptions and implement effective mitigation and recovery plans.
- Monitor demand, forecasts and order books to ensure material availability and minimise supply chain disruption.
- Manage supplier performance, challenging suppliers where necessary and driving corrective actions to improve delivery.
- Lead supplier recovery activities, coordinating internal teams and external suppliers to resolve issues and restore supply.
- Manage purchasing and ordering requirements, ensuring appropriate ordering strategies and stock levels are maintained.
- Maintain accurate MRP master data and manage order books using SAP and other supply chain systems.
- Prioritise supply chain requirements in line with operational and manufacturing demands.
- Act as the first point of contact for supply chain queries from internal operational teams.
- Build effective working relationships with suppliers, internal stakeholders and colleagues across international locations.
- Coordinate supplier working parties and collaborate with Procurement, Supply Chain Quality and Commercial teams.
- Use data management tools and digital solutions to support decision-making, automate processes and improve supply chain efficiency.
- Monitor and optimise procured goods stock, ensuring effective inventory management.
- Support supply chain transformation projects, continuous improvement initiatives and the implementation of LEAN methodologies.

Skills & Experience Required

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Previous experience within Supply Chain, Procurement, Manufacturing Engineering or Design Engineering.
- Experience managing suppliers, supplier performance or material availability within a manufacturing environment.
- Strong understanding of Material Requirements Planning (MRP) and experience using SAP within manufacturing or supply chain operations.
- Experience managing purchase orders, order books, forecasts and inventory.
- Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify supply chain risks and implement effective solutions.
- Experience using digital tools, data management systems or process automation to improve operational efficiency.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to communicate across all levels of the business.
- Experience working with international suppliers or within a global, cross-functional environment.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- A collaborative approach, with a proactive attitude towards continuous improvement.

Desirable Experience
- Project management experience.
- Knowledge or experience of LEAN methodologies.
- Experience leading supplier recovery plans or supplier improvement initiatives.
- Experience supporting supply chain transformation or digitalisation projects.
- Flexibility and willingness to travel to supplier locations when required.

Finance AdministratorLocation: Larne Full-time Permanent
Your New CompanyHays is delighted to be working with an established and successful organisation in the Larne area to recruit a Finance Administrator to join their finance team.This is an excellent opportunity for someone with Accounts Payable or broader finance administration experience who is looking to develop their career within a professional and well-structured finance environment. - Ensuring finance processes are completed in line with internal controls, policies and relevant regulations.
- Identifying and escalating discrepancies or potential issues where appropriate.
- Supporting ongoing improvements and efficiencies within Accounts Payable and wider finance processes.
- Providing general administrative support and assisting with ad hoc finance and cross-functional projects when required.
